alignments.name: Newgrange
alignments.feature: Light enters through the roof-box above the entrance, runs up the 19 m passage and lights the floor of the inner chamber.
alignments.claim: Newgrange is built so that the rising sun on the days around the winter solstice shines through the roof-box into the chamber.
alignments.viewing: Inside the chamber on the solstice mornings only by the annual lottery at the Bru na Boinne Visitor Centre (60 winners); otherwise a guided tour with a simulated sunrise.

sources.title: Newgrange
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.quote: It is aligned so that the rising sun on the winter solstice shines through a "roofbox" above the entrance and floods the inner chamber.

sources.title: Newgrange
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.quote: To experience the phenomenon on the morning of the Winter Solstice from inside Newgrange, visitors to Bru Na Bóinne Visitor Centre must enter an annual lottery at the centre.

sources.title: Bru na Boinne Visitor Centre: Newgrange and Knowth
sources.author: OPW Heritage Ireland
sources.quote: Sunrise over Red Mountain in Donore where it shines across into the roof box at Newgrange.

sources.title: Newgrange
sources.author: Stone Pages
sources.quote: Above the entrance passage is a 'roof-box', which precisely aligns with the rising sun at the winter solstice of 21 December

alignments.name: Maeshowe
alignments.feature: The entrance passage faces south-west; the setting midwinter sun shines along it and lights the back wall of the chamber.
alignments.claim: For a few days either side of the winter solstice the setting sun shines down the passage of Maeshowe into the chamber.
alignments.viewing: Guided tours by Historic Environment Scotland; the midwinter sunset in the chamber is also shown on a webcam in December.

sources.title: Maeshowe
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.quote: The monument is aligned so that sunlight enters the passage at the winter solstice and reaches the rear wall of the central chamber.

sources.title: Maeshowe
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.quote: This entrance corridor is so placed that it lets the direct light of the setting sun into the chamber for a few days on each side of the winter solstice

sources.title: Maes Howe
sources.author: Stone Pages
sources.quote: The fact that the entrance faces SW suggests that the builders of Maes Howe had an interest in the winter sunset.

alignments.name: Stonehenge
alignments.feature: The axis of the stone settings, the north-east entrance and the Avenue run towards midsummer sunrise, close to the Heel Stone.
alignments.claim: Stonehenge's main axis points north-east to where the sun rises at the summer solstice, near the Heel Stone.
alignments.viewing: English Heritage opens the stones to the public at the summer and winter solstices and the equinoxes (managed access).

sources.title: Stonehenge
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.quote: At the Summer solstice an observer standing within the stone circle, looking northeast through the entrance, would see the Sun rise in the approximate direction of the Heel Stone

sources.title: Description of Stonehenge
sources.author: English Heritage
sources.quote: At midsummer, the sun rises over the horizon to the north-east, close to the Heel Stone.

sources.title: Stonehenge Avenue
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.quote: Along some of its length, the avenue is aligned with the sunrise of the summer solstice, suggesting a time of most frequent use.

alignments.name: Stonehenge
alignments.feature: Looking south-west along the axis, the midwinter sun set in the gap of the Great Trilithon, the tallest of the five trilithons.
alignments.claim: The same axis, read the other way, points to the winter solstice sunset, which may have been the more important event.
alignments.viewing: English Heritage opens the stones to the public at the winter solstice (managed access).

sources.title: Stonehenge
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.quote: are aligned to the sunset of the winter solstice and the opposing sunrise of the summer solstice

sources.title: Description of Stonehenge
sources.author: English Heritage
sources.quote: At midwinter, the sun sets in the south-west, in the gap between the two tallest trilithons, one of which has now fallen.

sources.title: Significance of Stonehenge
sources.author: English Heritage
sources.quote: At the centre of this belief system was the sun, with the solstice alignments enshrined within the fabric of the monument.

alignments.name: Bryn Celli Ddu
alignments.feature: The passage of the passage tomb faces the midsummer sunrise; light reaches the back of the chamber for some weeks around the solstice.
alignments.claim: At sunrise around the summer solstice, light shines down the passage of Bryn Celli Ddu into its chamber.
alignments.viewing: Cadw site, open all year; Cadw holds summer solstice sunrise openings.

sources.title: Bryn Celli Ddu
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.quote: The passage is roughly aligned with the Summer Solstice sunrise, such that for some weeks around the summer solstice, sunlight can find its way through to the back wall of the burial chamber.

sources.title: Bryn Celli Ddu Burial Chamber
sources.author: Cadw
sources.quote: As the sun rises on the summer solstice (the longest day of the year) shafts of light shine directly down the tomb

alignments.name: Loughcrew Cairn T
alignments.feature: Sunlight at the spring and autumn equinox sunrise enters the passage of Cairn T and lights the decorated backstone of the end chamber.
alignments.claim: Cairn T at Loughcrew is aligned so that the equinox sunrise lights the carved backstone inside the chamber.
alignments.viewing: OPW opens the cairn at the spring and autumn equinoxes, when people gather at sunrise; key from the Loughcrew coffee shop in summer.

sources.title: Loughcrew
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.quote: Cairn T in Carnbane East is directed to receive the beams of the rising sun on the spring and autumnal equinox - the light shining down the passage and illuminating the art on the backstone.

sources.title: Loughcrew Cairns
sources.author: OPW Heritage Ireland
sources.quote: The cairn is aligned to sunrise at the spring and autumn equinoxes and at these times people gather there to greet the first rays of the sun.

alignments.name: Dowth
alignments.feature: The evening sun enters the passage of Dowth South and lights three stones of its circular chamber around the winter solstice.
alignments.claim: Dowth South is lit by the setting sun in the winter months, most fully around the winter solstice: a sunset counterpart of Newgrange.
alignments.viewing: Dowth is open access; the chambers are closed to the public.

sources.title: Dowth
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.quote: From November to February, the rays of the evening sun reach into the passage and then the chamber of Dowth South.

sources.title: Brú na Bóinne
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.quote: Newgrange and Dowth have winter solstice solar alignments, while Knowth is oriented towards the March equinox (spring equinox) and the September equinox (autumn equinox).

alignments.name: Knowth
alignments.feature: The eastern passage of the great mound of Knowth faces the equinox sunrise.
alignments.claim: The eastern passage at Knowth may be aligned on the equinox sunrise, but the alignment cannot now be shown.
views: The east-west passages point to the equinox sunrise and sunset, as Martin Brennan argued.
The passage entrances were altered by later souterrains and modern works, so it is hard to show an alignment ever existed.
alignments.viewing: Knowth is visited by guided tour from the Bru na Boinne Visitor Centre; the passages are closed.

sources.title: Knowth
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.quote: The east–west orientation of the passages at Knowth suggests astronomical alignment with the equinoxes.

sources.title: Knowth

sources.quote: the original entrances to the passages were distorted or destroyed, making it difficult to establish if an alignment ever existed.

alignments.name: Knowth
alignments.feature: The western passage of the great mound of Knowth faces the equinox sunset.
alignments.claim: The western passage at Knowth may be aligned on the equinox sunset, but the alignment cannot now be shown.
views: The east-west passages point to the equinox sunrise and sunset, as Martin Brennan argued.
The passage entrances were altered by later souterrains and modern works, so it is hard to show an alignment ever existed.
alignments.viewing: Knowth is visited by guided tour from the Bru na Boinne Visitor Centre; the passages are closed.

sources.title: Knowth

alignments.name: Drombeg stone circle
alignments.feature: The axis from the two portal stones across the recumbent stone points south-west to a notch in the hills where the midwinter sun sets.
alignments.claim: Drombeg's axis is set on the winter solstice sunset; the alignment is good but not exact.
alignments.viewing: Open access, signposted from the R597 near Glandore.

sources.title: Drombeg stone circle
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.quote: This arrangement creates a south-west axis, and orients the monument in the direction of the setting sun during the midwinter solstice.

sources.title: Drombeg
sources.author: Stone Pages
sources.quote: The midpoint of this stone was set in line with the winter soltice sunset viewed in a conspicuous notch in the distant hills; the alignment is good but not precise.

alignments.name: Balnuaran of Clava
alignments.feature: The passages of the north-east and south-west passage graves are in line and point south-west to the midwinter sunset.
alignments.claim: The two passage cairns at Balnuaran of Clava face the midwinter sunset, as do the passages of Clava cairns in general.
alignments.viewing: Historic Environment Scotland site, open access all year.

sources.title: Clava Cairns

alignments.name: Calanais (Callanish) Standing Stones
alignments.feature: Looking south along the stone avenue, the midsummer full moon at a major standstill skims the hills and sets behind Clisham.
alignments.claim: The Calanais avenue may have been laid out to watch the low southern moon at the major lunar standstill every 18.6 years.
views: Thom, Hawkins and later writers read the avenue and the hills of Harris as marking the moon at its major standstill.
Critics say alignments arise by chance in so many stones, and weathering and moved stones make any alignment uncertain.
alignments.viewing: Historic Environment Scotland site with a visitor centre; open access; crowds gather at major standstills (2006, 2024-25).

sources.title: Calanais

alignments.name: Easter Aquhorthies
alignments.feature: The level top of the recumbent stone, between its two flankers, lines up with the southern moonset towards the Hill of Fare.
alignments.claim: Easter Aquhorthies, a recumbent stone circle, faces the setting of the southern moon.
views: Burl and Ruggles found the recumbent stones of Aberdeenshire face the southern moon, framed between the flankers at the major standstill.
Bradley's excavation at Tomnaverie showed the circles were built around older cairns, which makes precise lunar observation unlikely.
alignments.viewing: Historic Environment Scotland site, open access.

views: Burl and Ruggles found the recumbent stones of Aberdeenshire face the southern moon, framed between the flankers at the major standstill.
Bradley's excavation at Tomnaverie showed the circles were built around older cairns, which makes precise lunar observation unlikely.
alignments.viewing: Historic Environment Scotland site, open access.

alignments.name: Tomnaverie stone circle
alignments.feature: The recumbent faces 233° (the perpendicular on the RCAHMS plan; 236-240° by other measures) towards Lochnagar, 30 km away, where the moon sets at the minor standstill.
alignments.claim: Tomnaverie's recumbent marks the set of the midsummer full moon at the minor standstill over Lochnagar, though its excavator later doubted this mattered.
views: Burl and Ruggles found the recumbent aligned on Lochnagar and the midsummer full moon setting there at the minor standstill.
Bradley showed the cairn came before the circle, and Ruggles now finds observing the moon from inside the circle difficult if not impossible.
alignments.viewing: Historic Environment Scotland site, open access.

alignments.name: Long Meg and Her Daughters
alignments.feature: The red sandstone outlier Long Meg stands south-west of the circle, on the line from the centre to the midwinter sunset.
alignments.claim: Long Meg, the outlying stone, marks the direction of the midwinter sunset seen from the centre of the circle.
alignments.viewing: Open access beside a minor road near Little Salkeld.

alignments.name: Ballochroy standing stones
alignments.feature: The central stone's flat face points across the Sound of Jura to Cora Bheinn, behind which Thom placed the midsummer sunset.
alignments.claim: Thom argued that the Ballochroy stones point to distant Jura peaks to mark the midsummer sunset precisely.
views: Thom: the distant Jura peaks give a precise solstice foresight.
Ruggles and others question Thom's selection of data, and the use of the stones remains controversial.
alignments.viewing: Visible from the A83 in Kintyre; on farmland.

sources.title: Ballochroy

alignments.name: Kintraw
alignments.feature: The 4 m standing stone and a stone platform across the gorge look to a notch between peaks of Jura where Thom placed a double midwinter sunset.
alignments.claim: Thom proposed Kintraw as a precise midwinter sunset observatory; MacKie's excavation found the platform he predicted, but critics remain unconvinced.
views: Thom and MacKie: Kintraw was an accurate winter solstice sunset site, with an artificial observation platform.
Ruggles and others: Thom's data were selected and horizon refraction limits the accuracy claimed; the platform's petrofabric analysis was inconclusive.
alignments.viewing: Beside the A816 north of Kilmartin.
